sentences.text: Dated this the 10th day of April, 2025 Petitioner's vehicle bearing No.KL-41-L-8813 was seized by the Police in connection with Crime No.1622 of 2024, registered at the Aluva East Police Station, for offences punishable under Sections 281 and 125(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 146 read with Section 196 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The crime is registered on the allegation that, rash and negligent driving of the vehicle led to an accident, resulting in the de facto complainant sustaining injuries.

The petitioner's application for interim custody of the vehicle was allowed by the Jurisdictional Magistrate as per Annexure A1 order, subject to the petitioner depositing cash security of Rs.2,50,000/-.
This Crl.M.C. is filed seeking deletion of the said condition.
2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the reason for imposing such onerous condition is absence of a valid insurance policy for the vehicle at the time of accident.

It is submitted that no issue of payment of 2025:KER:32224 CRL.MC NO. 2643 OF 2025 compensation to the de facto complainant, on his filing a claim petition before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, would arise since the petitioner has paid substantial amount to the de facto complainant towards the loss and hardship suffered by him due to the accident.
In this regard, attention is drawn to Annexure A3 receipt and the affidavit filed by the 2nd respondent.
3. The learned Public Prosecutor submitted that the 2nd respondent has vouched about the authenticity of the settlement and the affidavit filed by him.

4. As the 2nd respondent does not have any subsisting grievance and has submitted that he has no intention of claiming any further amount from the petitioner, the condition requiring deposit of cash security of Rs.2,50,000/- is unnecessary.
